match.reason: None of the three bank points teaches where people in money trouble can get help, such as hardship arrangements, free financial counsellors or bankruptcy, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Help with financial difficulty
card: Hardship arrangement
a request to your lender for changed terms when you cannot keep up repayments. The lender may pause repayments or lower them for a time.
Financial counsellor
a trained person who helps you sort out debts and plan a way forward. The service is free and confidential, and you can use it before your debts get out of hand.
Bankruptcy
a legal process for people who cannot pay their debts. It is a last resort, because it can limit what the person can do with money for years.
It is usually best to ask for help early. Lenders and counsellors have more options when a person acts before missing many payments.
draft.remember: Ask early: talk to your lender, see a free counsellor, and keep bankruptcy as the last resort.

a.q: Jo has lost shifts at work and may miss her car loan repayments next month. What is a sensible first step?
opts: Ask the lender for a hardship arrangement
Declare bankruptcy straight away
Ignore the loan until the lender contacts her
Take out a new loan to cover the repayments
a.why: A hardship arrangement lets the lender change the terms while Jo cannot keep up. Bankruptcy is wrong as a first step because it is a last resort with long effects.
a.clue: Which step is made to your lender, before things get worse?

b.q: Sam has debts from several sources and is not sure what he can afford to repay. He does not want to pay a fee for advice. What should he do?
opts: See a free financial counsellor to plan his debts
Go bankrupt so that all his debts disappear
Pay a company to arrange the debts for him
Wait until he misses many payments before acting
b.why: A financial counsellor is free and helps people sort out debts and plan. Bankruptcy is a tempting wrong answer, but it is a last resort with long effects and not the first step.
b.clue: Look for the help that costs nothing and comes before drastic steps.

a.best: Ask the lender for a hardship arrangement

b.best: See a free financial counsellor to plan his debts
